LanguageData.CC_Feast_Ans_Yes_4: {NAME} sends back a yes, and a warning that their people eat a great deal. Expect them for {FEAST}.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Ans_YesHope_3: {NAME} will come to {FEAST}. That there will be {HOPE} settled it.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Ans_YesHope_4: For {FEAST} with {HOPE}, {NAME} would walk twice as far, and will come.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Ans_No_4: {NAME} can't come to {FEAST}. The answer is polite, and short.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Ans_Moot_3: Things at the colony moved on before the answer came, and the letter about {FEAST} is answered with thanks and nothing more.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Set_4: Every answer is back, and {GUESTS} of {PEOPLES} are coming to {FEAST}. Expect them on {DATE}, or on the first fine day after it.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Arrive_4: The road has brought them: {GUESTS} of {PEOPLES}, here for {FEAST}, each with one or two of their own. They are making their way to the gate.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Arrive_Wedding_2: Kin and friends of the one who marries in have come for the wedding: {GUESTS} of {PEOPLES}, walking up to the gate with those who came with them.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Arrive_Wedding_3: Wedding guests at the gate: {GUESTS} of {PEOPLES}, each with one or two of their people. They will wait there until the ceremony, and sit at the colony's table after it.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Champion_Ours_3: {CHAMPION} won the most today, and the colony's own is named champion of {FEAST}.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Champion_Ours_4: Of everyone at {FEAST}, {CHAMPION} won the most, and the honor of the day stays at home.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Champion_Guest_3: {CHAMPION} of {PEOPLE} won the most today and is named champion of {FEAST}. The guests will have a story for the road home.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Champion_Guest_4: The honor of the day goes home with the guests: {CHAMPION} of {PEOPLE} is named champion of {FEAST}.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Msg_Sour_4: {GUEST} has had enough of {PAWN}, or of the drink, and the two are trading blows after the feast.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_End_3: {GUESTS} left at first light, the road home ahead of them and {FEAST} behind.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_End_4: The guests are gone, out through the gate at first light: {GUESTS}, home from {FEAST}.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_End_Insulted_2: {GUESTS} did not wait for first light. They left {FEAST} offended, and their people will hear why.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_End_Insulted_3: Offended at how they were kept, {GUESTS} have walked out of {FEAST} early.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Died_2: {NAME} of {PEOPLE} came as a guest to {FEAST} and has died at the colony. The other guests are going home, and {PEOPLE} will want to know how it happened.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Suggest_3: {PAWN}, the steward, has looked over the stores and the land and found both in good order: a season for {FEAST} with guests. {NAME} of {PEOPLE} might come, if asked.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Suggest_4: Guests, {PAWN} suggests: the colony can afford {FEAST} this season, and {NAME} of {PEOPLE} thinks well enough of it to come.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Away_Won_3: {PAWN} came home from the feast in {PLACE} with a win to tell: first in {CONTEST}, against the best {PEOPLE} had.
LanguageData.CC_Feast_Away_Won_4: Ask {PAWN} about the feast in {PLACE} and you'll hear about {CONTEST}, which {PAWN_pronoun} won against the best of {PEOPLE}.
